summary.name: Citadel
summary.one_liner: Citadel is an open source groupware and collaboration server offering email, calendaring, address books, forums, mailing lists, instant messaging, wiki/blog engines and RSS aggregation, accessed through a web UI or terminal client.
use_cases: Self-host email and collaboration for a small organization
Sync calendars and contacts with GroupDAV or WebDAV clients
Run internal forums and mailing lists
Host a wiki, blog or RSS reader for a group
Provide a BBS-style terminal client for users
summary.what_it_does: Citadel is a server system for email, collaboration and groupware, with the server (citserver) as its core and WebCit as the web interface. WebCit gives users and administrators browser access and also lets GroupDAV and Webcal (DAV) clients connect. An optional terminal client provides a BBS-style interface. The page lists supporting libraries: Berkeley DB as primary data store, libical for calendars, Expat for RSS and XMPP, libcurl, and OpenSSL for encrypted protocols. Citadel is distributed as source tarballs, with Easy Install and pre-built packages handling dependencies, and the project uses a rolling release model with a Git repository for development sources.
notable: Web UI (WebCit) also serves GroupDAV and Webcal (DAV) clients
Rolling release model; version-numbered manifest offered for packagers
Community add-ons include SELinux integration, Perl/PHP/Go client libraries and CitadelSync
Licensed GPL-3.0 per the awesome-selfhosted listing
caveats: WebCit will not run by itself and requires a working Citadel server
Development sources are unreleased code and should not be used for production systems
